title: Lead Generation Strategies That Work – Convert Traffic into Customers
description: Proven lead generation strategies for small businesses: CTAs, landing pages, forms, and content upgrades that turn visitors into leads.
content:
Lead Generation Strategies That Work

You’ve worked hard to get traffic to your website. Now it’s time to turn that traffic into leads and customers. Here are five proven strategies I use with my clients.

Watch this overview of effective lead generation tactics.

1. Create a Compelling Lead Magnet

Offer something valuable in exchange for an email address – a free ebook, checklist, or discount code. Make sure it’s directly related to what your audience wants.

2. Use Clear, Action‑Oriented CTAs

Your calls‑to‑action should stand out and tell visitors exactly what to do. “Get Your Free Quote” works better than “Submit.”

3. Optimize Your Forms

Keep forms short (name and email is often enough). Place them above the fold and use trust signals like “We never spam.”

4. Design Dedicated Landing Pages

For each campaign, create a landing page with a single goal. Remove navigation links to keep visitors focused.

5. Add Exit‑Intent Popups

When a user is about to leave, display a targeted offer. Done right, this can capture up to 10% of abandoning visitors.

title: SEO Friendly Website Design – Actionable Tips & Best Practices
description: Learn how to create an SEO friendly website with actionable tips on page speed, keyword placement, and technical SEO from an expert designer.
content:
SEO Friendly Website Design: A Practical Guide

You want a website that not only looks good but also appears on the first page of Google. In this guide, I’ll share my proven process for SEO friendly website design—the same techniques I use for all my clients.

Watch this quick guide on building SEO‑friendly websites.

1. Start with Keyword Research

Before writing a single line of code, research what your potential customers are searching for. This informs the page structure, headings, and content. For example, if you’re a local plumber, target phrases like “emergency plumber near me” and “plumbing services [City].”

2. Build a Solid Technical Foundation

Search engines need to crawl and index your site easily. Ensure:

  • Clean, semantic HTML with proper heading hierarchy (H1, H2, etc.).
  • Fast loading times (image optimization, minification, caching).
  • Mobile responsiveness (Google’s mobile‑first indexing).
  • XML sitemap and robots.txt.

3. On-Page SEO Elements

Every page gets unique title tags, meta descriptions, and URLs that include target keywords. Use internal linking to pass authority between pages—like linking this article to my SEO-optimized website & monthly SEO page.

4. Content That Answers Questions

Google loves helpful content. Write articles, FAQs, and service pages that address your customers’ pain points. This builds trust and improves dwell time—a positive ranking signal.

5. Ongoing Optimization

SEO isn’t a one‑time task. Set up analytics and monitor performance, making adjustments as needed. You’ll always know how your site is performing.

content:
How to Choose a Web Design Consultant

Hiring a web design consultant can be a game‑changer for your business – but only if you choose the right one. Here are key factors to consider before you book a session.

Learn what to ask before hiring a consultant.

1. Look for Relevant Experience

Ask about past projects similar to yours. A consultant who has worked with small businesses in your industry will understand your challenges and opportunities better than a generalist.

2. Check Their Strategic Approach

A good consultant doesn’t just talk about design – they ask about your business goals, target audience, and marketing plans. They should offer a clear process for how they’ll help you.

3. Read Testimonials and Case Studies

Look for evidence of results. Did they help other businesses increase traffic, improve conversion rates, or save money on development?

4. Understand Their Communication Style

You’ll be working closely together, so make sure they explain things clearly and listen to your ideas. A free initial call is a great way to gauge compatibility.

5. Clarify Deliverables and Pricing

Will you receive a written report? A strategy document? Ongoing support? Know exactly what you’re paying for.
